items: A young traveler steps toward the edge of a cliff with eyes on the sky, a small bundle over one shoulder, a white rose in hand and a little dog at their heels. The sun is bright and the whole road lies ahead. The card asks what you would try if you trusted yourself a little more, and whether your next step deserves a quick glance at the ground first.
beginnings, trust, spontaneity

A figure stands at a table, one hand raising a wand toward the sky and the other pointing down to the earth. On the table lie a cup, a sword, a pentacle and a wand, and an infinity sign floats above his head. The card asks you to notice the tools already within reach and to put your attention where your intention is.
willpower, skill, focus, resourcefulness

A woman sits calmly between a dark pillar and a light one, a crescent moon at her feet and a half-hidden scroll in her lap. Behind her hangs a veil sewn with pomegranates, with water just visible beyond it. She asks you to slow down and listen to what you already sense, even if you cannot yet put it into words.
intuition, mystery, stillness, inner knowing

A woman rests on soft cushions in a field of ripening wheat, with a stream and a forest behind her and a heart-shaped shield bearing the sign of Venus at her side. She wears a crown of stars and a gown patterned with pomegranates. The card invites you to tend what is growing in your life, to enjoy your senses and to let things ripen in their own time.
abundance, nurture, creativity, nature

A bearded ruler sits on a stone throne carved with rams' heads, holding a scepter and an orb, with bare red mountains behind him and armor showing beneath his robe. He stands for order, protection and the rules that keep things running. The card asks where a clear structure or a firm boundary would help you, and where control has hardened into stiffness.
structure, authority, stability, responsibility

A religious teacher sits between two pillars with one hand raised in blessing, two crossed keys at his feet and two followers kneeling before him. He stands for shared beliefs, ritual and the wisdom handed from one generation to the next. The card asks what you have learned from those who came before you, and which of their rules still feel true.
tradition, guidance, belonging, learning

A man and a woman stand unclothed beneath a winged angel and a blazing sun. Behind the woman grows a tree with a serpent wound around it, and behind the man a tree of flames. The card speaks of closeness and of choosing in line with what you truly value, in love and well beyond it.
union, values, choice, connection

A crowned charioteer stands in a canopied chariot pulled by two sphinxes, one black and one white, with a walled city behind him. He holds no reins and steers by will alone. The card asks you to bring together the parts of you that pull in different directions and move forward with purpose.
determination, drive, willpower, victory

A woman in white calmly holds the jaws of a lion, an infinity sign above her head and a chain of flowers linking her to the animal. There is no struggle here, only steady and gentle strength. The card asks you to meet what is wild in yourself or in others with patience rather than force.
courage, patience, compassion, gentleness

An old man in a gray cloak stands alone on a snowy peak, leaning on a staff and holding up a lantern with a six-pointed star inside. His light reaches only the next few steps of the path. The card invites a quieter stretch of time, away from the noise, to hear your own thoughts and find your own way.
solitude, reflection, wisdom, inner guidance

A great wheel marked with letters and symbols turns in the sky, with a sphinx seated on top, a snake sliding down one side and a jackal-headed figure rising on the other. In the four corners, winged creatures read from open books among the clouds. The card reminds you that life moves in cycles and asks how you can meet this turn with open eyes.
cycles, change, luck, turning point

A figure in red sits between two pillars, holding an upright sword in one hand and a pair of scales in the other, with a calm and direct gaze. Nothing is hidden from that look. The card asks you to weigh things honestly, to look at cause and effect, and to own your part in what happened.
fairness, truth, accountability, balance

A man hangs upside down by one foot from a T-shaped cross of living wood, his other leg bent behind the first to form a figure four and his hands tucked behind his back. His face is calm and a halo glows around his head. The card asks whether a pause, or looking at things from a completely different angle, might show you what pushing ahead cannot.
surrender, pause, new perspective, letting go

A skeleton in black armor rides a white horse and carries a black banner marked with a white rose, while a king lies fallen and a child and a bishop turn to face him. On the horizon the sun shines between two towers. Rather than a literal death, the card speaks of a chapter closing so that something new can begin, and asks what you are ready to let go of.
endings, transformation, release, renewal

A winged angel stands with one foot on land and one in a pool, pouring water back and forth between two cups. A path leads from the water toward a crown of light on distant mountains, and irises bloom close by. The card invites you to find the middle way, combining different parts of your life with patience until they work together.
balance, moderation, patience, blending

A horned, bat-winged figure crouches on a dark pedestal with an inverted star above his brow, while a naked man and woman stand chained below him. The chains around their necks hang loose enough to lift off. The card asks you to look at what holds you in place, whether a pattern, a belief or a craving for more, and to notice how much of that hold you could loosen yourself.
attachment, temptation, shadow self, restriction

Lightning strikes a tall tower on a rocky peak and knocks off its crown, while flames burst from the windows and two figures fall headlong. Small sparks of light drift through the dark sky around it. The card speaks of sudden change that topples whatever was built on weak ground, and asks what truth might be revealed once the dust settles.
upheaval, revelation, sudden change, breakthrough

Beneath one large eight-pointed star and seven smaller ones, a naked woman kneels by a pool, pouring water from one jug into the pool and from the other onto the land. A bird rests in a tree behind her. After a hard season, the card invites quiet hope and asks you to trust that you can heal and begin again.
hope, renewal, serenity, inspiration

A full moon with a calm face in profile hangs between two towers, shedding drops of light over a winding path. A dog and a wolf howl up at it, and a crayfish crawls out of a pool in the foreground. The card speaks of uncertainty, dreams and half-seen fears, and asks you to move slowly and feel your way until the picture becomes clear.
illusion, dreams, the unconscious, uncertainty

A bright sun with a face shines over a garden wall lined with sunflowers. Below it, a naked child rides a white horse with arms open wide, carrying a red banner. The card celebrates warmth, clarity and simple happiness, and asks you to let yourself enjoy what is going well.
joy, success, vitality, warmth

An angel blows a trumpet from the clouds, and below, men, women and children rise from their coffins with arms open to greet the call. Snow-capped mountains stand behind them. The card asks you to look back on your past with honesty and kindness, and to answer a call that feels like a fresh start.
reckoning, calling, rebirth, forgiveness

A dancer wrapped loosely in a purple sash floats inside a large oval wreath, holding a wand in each hand. In the four corners are an angel, an eagle, a lion and a bull, the same figures seen on the Wheel of Fortune. The card marks a cycle brought to a full close and asks you to take in how far you have come before the next journey begins.
completion, wholeness, achievement, integration

A hand reaches out of a cloud holding a living wand, fresh leaves still sprouting from the wood. Below, a river winds past a castle on a far hill. The card offers a spark: an idea, a wish or a burst of drive that wants to be used while it is warm. It asks what you would start if you trusted that first flicker of enthusiasm.
spark, inspiration, new energy

A man stands on the walls of his castle, a small globe in one hand and a wand in the other, a second wand fixed beside him. He looks out over sea and land, weighing what he already has against what lies beyond. The card invites you to choose a direction and balance comfort against the pull of something bigger.
planning, choice, wider horizons

Seen from behind, a figure stands on a high ridge among three planted wands, watching ships move across the water below. Plans have been set in motion and the first of them are already under way. The card asks you to look further ahead and welcome help from others as your efforts begin to bear fruit.
expansion, foresight, first results

Four wands stand in the foreground with a garland of flowers and fruit hung across them, like a gate or a canopy. Behind it, two figures lift bouquets in welcome, and a castle rises in the distance. The card marks a firm foundation worth celebrating, a moment to rest and enjoy what has been built before moving on.
celebration, home, stability

Five young men swing their wands at one another in a crowded scuffle that looks half like a fight and half like a game. No one seems to be winning and no one is badly hurt. The card points to clashing wills and noisy rivalry, and asks whether the struggle is sharpening you or just wearing you out.
competition, friction, challenge

A rider on a white horse wears a laurel wreath, and another wreath is tied to the top of his wand. People walk alongside him carrying their own wands, as if in a small parade. The card speaks of progress that others can see, and invites you to accept praise graciously and share the credit.
recognition, progress, confidence

A man on higher ground holds his wand across his body against six wands rising toward him from below. His mismatched footwear suggests he was caught by surprise, yet he keeps his footing. The card asks you to weigh what is truly worth defending and then hold your position with patience.
standing firm, perseverance, conviction

Eight wands fly through clear air in parallel lines, slanting down toward open country and a river below. There are no people on the card, only motion. It speaks of a moment when things move fast, and it invites you to aim your energy in one direction and let it travel.
movement, speed, focus

A man with a bandaged head leans on his wand and glances warily to the side, eight more wands standing behind him like a fence. He has been through a hard stretch and is still on his feet. The card honors that endurance while asking you to notice whether caution is protecting you or keeping you from the last few steps.
resilience, persistence, guardedness

A man bends forward under a bundle of ten wands, his face hidden behind them as he trudges toward a town. He has nearly arrived, but the load has become all he can see. The card invites you to look at what you are carrying, finish what matters and set down what was never yours to hold.
burden, responsibility, completion

A young figure in a tunic patterned with salamanders stands in a bare desert, gazing up at the tall wand in their hands. Distant pyramids sit on the horizon. The card brings a beginner's excitement, a fresh message or idea, and invites you to explore it without needing to be an expert yet.
curiosity, enthusiasm, news

A knight on a rearing horse rides through the desert, the plume on his helmet flickering like a flame and his tunic marked with salamanders. He holds his wand high and seems eager to be anywhere but standing still. The card celebrates daring and momentum, and asks you to act with energy while keeping enough care not to burn out.
action, adventure, boldness

A queen sits on a throne carved with lions, a wand in one hand and a sunflower in the other, with a black cat at her feet. She looks out with open, sunny self-possession. The card invites you to lead with warmth and trust your own light, steady enough in yourself to make others feel welcome.
warmth, confidence, self-assurance

A king sits on a throne decorated with lions and salamanders, holding a flowering wand, while a small salamander rests at his feet. He leans slightly forward, as if already seeing the next move. The card speaks of seasoned, inspiring leadership and asks you to hold a clear vision and carry it through with integrity.
vision, leadership, initiative

A hand reaches from a cloud holding a cup that overflows in five streams into a pond of water lilies below. A dove descends toward the cup carrying a small wafer. The card offers a fresh opening of the heart, a new love, friendship or tenderness, and invites you to receive it as freely as it pours.
open heart, new feeling, tenderness

A young man and woman face each other and exchange cups, as if making a promise. Above them floats a staff entwined with two snakes and crowned with a winged lion's head. The card speaks of a meeting of equals, and asks you to notice what a relationship needs in order to stay balanced and kind.
partnership, connection, mutual respect

Three women dance in a circle and raise their cups in a toast, with fruit and flowers from the harvest at their feet. Their joy comes from being together. The card invites you to share good moments with the people who stand by you, and to notice what grows when you work and celebrate side by side.
friendship, community, joy

A young man sits under a tree with his arms crossed, staring at three cups set before him on the grass. A hand from a cloud offers him a fourth cup, which he does not seem to see. The card points to a pause that can be restful or simply stale, and asks whether something good is being offered while you look elsewhere.
withdrawal, contemplation, missed offer

A figure in a black cloak bows over three spilled cups, while two cups still stand upright behind him. Across the river, a bridge leads toward a small castle. The card gives room to sorrow and loss, and gently asks you, in your own time, to turn around and see what is still standing.
grief, disappointment, what remains

In an old courtyard, a child hands a smaller child a cup filled with white flowers, and more flowering cups stand nearby. The scene feels like a warm memory. The card speaks of simple generosity and the comfort of the past, and invites you to bring that gentleness into the present.
nostalgia, kindness, innocence

A dark figure faces seven cups floating on a cloud, each holding a different vision: a face, a veiled glowing figure, a snake, a castle, jewels, a laurel wreath and a dragon. Some look like treasures and some like warnings. The card asks you to step back and assess which dreams are real possibilities and which are only daydreams.
daydreams, options, illusion

Under a watchful moon, a cloaked figure with a staff walks away from eight neatly stacked cups toward rocky hills. Nothing looks broken, yet something is missing from the arrangement. The card speaks of the courage to leave what no longer fulfills you and to focus on a deeper search, even when the road ahead is unclear.
walking away, seeking more, moving on

A well-fed man sits on a bench with his arms folded and a satisfied smile, nine cups lined up on a draped shelf behind him. Often called the wish card, it shows comfort and pleasure close at hand. It invites you to enjoy how far you have come, while asking whether what you wished for truly nourishes you.
contentment, satisfaction, wishes

A couple stands with arms around each other, raising their hands toward a rainbow of ten cups, while two children dance beside them. A small house sits among green hills. The card speaks of lasting emotional fulfillment, and invites you to notice the everyday moments where love feels like home.
harmony, family, fulfillment

A young figure in a flower-patterned tunic stands by the sea, looking at a cup from which a small fish peeks out. The page seems delighted rather than alarmed. The card brings a gentle surprise, a creative idea or a tender message, and invites you to stay open to feelings that arrive in unexpected ways.
imagination, sensitivity, pleasant surprise

A knight on a white horse rides calmly forward, holding a cup out in front of him like an offering. Small wings rise from his helmet and heels, and a stream runs through the land ahead. The card speaks of offers made from the heart, and asks you to follow your ideals while keeping your feet on the ground.
romance, invitation, following the heart

A queen sits on a carved throne at the very edge of the sea, gazing into an ornate, closed cup. She seems to listen inwardly to what the cup holds. The card invites you to care deeply for yourself and others, trusting your intuition while keeping healthy boundaries.
compassion, intuition, emotional care

A king sits on a throne set on a stone block in the middle of a restless sea, a cup in one hand and a scepter in the other. A ship sails on one side and a dolphin leaps on the other, yet he stays composed. The card speaks of feeling deeply without being swept away, and asks you to lead with a steady, generous heart.
emotional balance, calm, wisdom

A hand reaches out of a cloud holding a single upright sword, its tip passing through a crown hung with green sprigs, high above bare gray peaks. It is the moment a thought cuts cleanly through the fog. The card asks you to name what you now see plainly and to use that clarity fairly.
clarity, breakthrough, truth, a sharp idea

A blindfolded woman sits by the shore with two heavy swords crossed over her heart, a crescent moon above and rocks breaking the water behind her. She holds perfectly still, keeping both options at arm's length. The card asks what you are choosing not to look at, and whether this truce with yourself is a rest or a way of putting off a decision.
stalemate, a hard choice, avoidance, truce

Three swords pierce a red heart against a sky of gray cloud and slanting rain. It is one of the plainest images in the deck: something hurt, and now it is out in the open. The card invites you to let the sadness be real, knowing that rain passes and that a named pain is easier to tend than a hidden one.
heartache, grief, painful truth, release

A knight lies carved in stone on a tomb, hands joined in prayer, with three swords hanging point-down on the wall above him and a fourth lying lengthwise along the side of the tomb, while a stained-glass window glows nearby. This is not an ending but deep rest, the stillness that lets a tired mind mend. The card suggests stepping back and giving yourself a real pause before the next round.
rest, recovery, retreat, quiet

A man with a sly half-smile gathers up swords while two defeated figures walk off toward the water beneath a sky of torn clouds. Someone has won, but the win looks lonely. The card asks whether being right is worth what it costs, and when it is wiser to lay the argument down.
conflict, hollow victory, pride, walking away

A ferryman poles a small boat across the water, carrying a hunched, cloaked figure and a child, with six swords standing upright in the bow. The water is choppy on one side and smooth on the other, and a quieter shore lies ahead. The card speaks of leaving a hard place behind, slowly and with help, carrying only what you need.
transition, moving on, passage, calmer waters

A man tiptoes away from a camp of tents with five swords in his arms, glancing back over his shoulder at the two he has left planted in the ground. He is clever and quick, but he is also slipping away from something. The card asks you to look honestly at any shortcut or secret, your own or someone else's, and at what might be left behind.
strategy, stealth, evasion, going it alone

A woman stands bound and blindfolded among eight swords planted in wet ground, a castle high on the cliff behind her. Her legs are free, and the swords do not fully close her in. The card suggests that some of what holds you is a story you keep telling yourself, and that one small step may reveal the gap.
feeling trapped, self-imposed limits, helplessness, a way out

A figure sits upright in bed in the dark, face buried in both hands, with nine swords lined up on the black wall behind. The quilt is patterned with roses and planetary signs, and the carving on the bed shows a struggle. This is the small-hours mind, where worries grow larger than they are; the card invites you to turn on the light, talk it through and see what is really there.
worry, sleepless nights, anxious thoughts, nightmares

A man lies face down by a still shore with ten swords in his back, a red cloth across him and a black sky overhead, yet a band of gold light is breaking on the horizon. It is a dramatic picture of something being completely over. The card's quiet message lies in that strip of light: when something is truly finished, there is room for a new day to begin.
rock bottom, a final ending, exhaustion, a new dawn

A young person stands on a windswept rise, sword raised in both hands, glancing sideways as clouds race and birds scatter overhead. They are alert, curious and eager to test every idea. The card encourages fresh questions and quick learning, with a reminder that a sharp tongue still needs a kind aim.
curiosity, vigilance, new ideas, sharp questions

A knight charges at full gallop on a white horse, sword thrust forward, while the wind tears at the trees and clouds behind him. He is all conviction and momentum, rushing straight at his goal. The card admires that drive and asks you to check where you are heading before you get there.
speed, conviction, charging ahead, directness

A queen sits in profile on a stone throne carved with butterflies, holding her sword upright while her other hand reaches out as if in welcome. Clouds gather below her and a single bird flies high above. She stands for clear sight and honest words earned through experience, and the card asks you to speak your truth with both precision and grace.
clear judgment, honesty, independence, boundaries

A king faces you squarely from his throne, sword held upright and slightly tilted, with butterflies and crescent moons carved behind him and tall trees in the distance. He rules by reason, principle and clear rules. The card asks you to decide with a cool head and a fair mind, without letting cleverness turn cold.
authority, intellect, fairness, principle

A hand reaches out of a cloud offering a single golden coin above a flowering garden, where a path leads through an arch of hedges toward distant mountains. It is the seed of something real and tangible, a resource or a chance to build. The card invites you to notice the practical opening in front of you and to plant it with care.
opportunity, prosperity, a seed, groundedness

A young man in a tall hat dances as he juggles two coins inside a looping ribbon shaped like a figure eight, while ships rise and fall on big waves behind him. He keeps everything moving with good humor. The card speaks of balancing several demands at once and asks which of them truly need your hands right now.
balance, juggling, adaptability, priorities

Inside a cathedral, a stonemason stands on a bench carving an arch while a monk and a figure holding the plans look on and talk it over, three coins worked into the stone above. Each brings a different skill to the same task. The card celebrates good craft and collaboration, and asks you to value what others add as the work takes shape.
teamwork, craft, collaboration, skill

A crowned man sits outside a city, clutching one coin to his chest, with another balanced on his head and two pinned under his feet. He is safe, but he can barely move. The card asks what you are holding on to so tightly, and whether security has started to feel more like a wall than a home.
security, holding on, control, saving

Two figures in rags trudge through falling snow, one on crutches, past a church window glowing with five coins in its stained glass. They are cold and fixed on the struggle, and do not seem to notice the light just above them. The card acknowledges hard times and feeling shut out, and gently points to support that may be closer than it looks.
hardship, feeling left out, struggle, help nearby

A well-dressed merchant holds a pair of scales in one hand and drops coins into the open palm of a kneeling person, while a second person waits beside them. Six coins hang in the air around the scene. The card looks at giving and receiving, and asks whether the exchanges in your life feel balanced, and on which side of the scales you stand today.
generosity, giving and receiving, fairness, sharing

A young farmer rests on his hoe and gazes at a leafy bush growing seven coins, as if weighing what all his work has produced. The harvest is not quite ready. The card invites a pause to take stock of your efforts, to be patient with slow growth and to decide where your energy is best spent next.
patience, investment, taking stock, slow growth

A craftsman sits at his bench, carefully hammering a design into a coin, while finished pieces hang on a post beside him and a town waits in the distance. He is absorbed, patient and getting better with every stroke. The card honors steady practice and asks you to give your full attention to the work in front of you.
diligence, practice, mastery, careful work

A woman in a robe patterned with flowers stands in a lush vineyard heavy with grapes, a hooded falcon resting on her gloved hand and a fine house behind her. Nine coins gleam among the vines. She has made a good life through her own effort and enjoys it on her own terms. The card invites you to savor what you have built and to trust your independence.
self-reliance, comfort, enjoyment, earned ease

In the foreground an old man in a richly patterned cloak sits with two dogs, while a couple talk beneath a stone archway and a child reaches out to one of the dogs, ten coins laid over the scene in a careful pattern. Three generations share one home. The card speaks of roots, family and what lasts beyond a single lifetime, and asks what you would like to pass on.
legacy, family, lasting wealth, roots

A young person stands in a green spring field, holding a single coin up in both hands and studying it closely, with freshly plowed earth and trees behind. They are earnest, careful and ready to learn. The card points to the start of a practical project or course of study, and to the value of small, steady first steps.
study, a new venture, diligence, practical curiosity

A knight sits on a heavy, motionless horse at the edge of a plowed field, holding a coin and regarding it calmly. Unlike the other knights, he is not charging anywhere. He stands for steady, dependable effort, and the card asks you to keep going methodically while making sure routine does not turn into a rut.
reliability, routine, patience, hard work

A queen sits in a flowering garden under an arch of roses, a coin cradled in her lap, her throne carved with fruit and goats' heads, while a rabbit sits in the grass in the corner. She is warm, sensible and at home in the physical world. The card speaks of caring for people and things in practical ways, and asks you to look after your own comfort as well as everyone else's.
nurture, practicality, abundance, warmth

A king sits on a throne decorated with bulls' heads, his robe covered in grapevines, a coin resting in one hand and a scepter in the other, with a castle rising behind him. He has built lasting security through patience and good judgment. The card asks you to lead with steadiness and to share generously what you have built.
abundance, security, discipline, generosity
